_comment: The generation manifest. Every thread that is not hand-written is specified here as beats, not prose. Generation fills in the words; this file decides what happens. Keeping the beats hand-authored is what stops the corpus from being a template.

_hours_key.business: 09:00-18:00 weekdays. Most routine traffic. This is what dilutes the second-shift ratio back toward true.

threads.subject: billing
threads.beats: Week 6. Dane makes the case for billing: two clinics asked, he thinks it closes the seed. Priya pushes back with the six-week estimate. It stays professional. Neither concedes. Ends unresolved with Dane saying they should talk Monday. Note that this happens AFTER Theo told her billing was a trapdoor on Apr 24 and BEFORE she tells Theo they cut it on May 18, so her position here should already be firm without her citing Theo.
constraints: Priya's messages get longer than usual for Dane, 30-60 words, which is itself a signal
Dane writes one long excited run-on message

threads.subject: Re: billing
threads.beats: Week 7. The one time it gets sharp. Dane says she is building for Rosalind and not for the market. Priya says he is selling a product that does not exist yet. Both are partly right. One message from each of them is slightly too honest. It does not become a fight, it becomes quiet, and the thread stops mid-exchange.
constraints: one message from Priya sent after midnight that is longer and more raw than anything else she sends Dane

threads.subject: scoping billing down
threads.beats: Week 9. The compromise, arrived at without either of them referencing the sharp exchange. Billing read-only, invoicing deferred to post-seed, scoped to two weeks. Dane is fine with it, which retroactively suggests the argument was never really about billing. Warm again by the end.
constraints: Dane sends one message that is just 'ok this is good'

threads.subject: sched v2
threads.beats: Design work for the room-based scheduler rewrite, running in parallel with the Rosalind crisis. Callum sends Figma links with no context. Priya replies 'this is right' or 'room block needs to read as a wall not a card'. One 2am message from Callum that is genuinely the sharpest thing anyone says about the product that month, about how a room is a place and an appointment is a promise and the UI was treating both as boxes.
constraints: the 2am message is 80-120 words and unlike everything else he sends

threads.subject: invoice
threads.beats: An invoice that should take two messages and takes eleven, spread over two months. Wrong PO number, a resend to the wrong address, a period where both assume the other is handling it, Callum apologizing for chasing, Priya apologizing for the delay. Nobody is at fault and it is nobody's priority. Resolves eventually with no ceremony.
constraints: at least one message that is just 'sorry just saw this'

threads.subject: Water in the rear bathroom
threads.beats: First flooding. Ezra explains it is not a plumbing issue, it is a drainage characteristic of the building. Numbers his points. Priya replies once, briefly. He gets the last word.

threads.subject: Water in the rear bathroom (2)
threads.beats: Second flooding. Still not a plumbing issue. Now it is a tenant usage pattern. Priya is slightly funnier than she means to be. Ezra does not notice. He gets the last word again.
constraints: Ezra references his own previous email as though it settled the matter

threads.subject: Rear bathroom, further to my previous
threads.beats: Third flooding. Ezra proposes a schedule of tenant responsibilities. It has five numbered items and the fifth is about the bathroom. Priya replies with one line. He gets the last word for the third time, which is the whole joke.

threads.subject: Northlane, and a role I think you'd want to hear about
threads.beats: Five inbound from Hana across the window, one reply from Priya in April saying she is not looking. Hana names Thicket each time to prove research. Each message is shorter and more direct than the last. The final one in June is two sentences and slightly wounded. Priya never replies again.
constraints: exactly one message from Priya, in April

threads.subject: room assignments thursday
threads.beats: The practical follow-through on the room migration Priya promised Rosalind. Beatriz is brisk and competent and slightly amused by the whole thing. Confirms the Thursday session, does the assignments, flags two rooms that are actually one room with a curtain, which is a real data modeling problem nobody anticipated.
constraints: the curtain detail is the thing that matters

threads.subject: saw the news
threads.beats: An old Corvia colleague sees the funding announcement, sends congratulations, they trade two messages of genuine warmth and one attempt to schedule a coffee that never gets scheduled. Then nothing for the rest of the window. Thin but real, which is exactly the case the reciprocity damper in the ranker exists to handle.

threads.subject: thursday check-in notes
threads.beats: Routine post-crisis check-ins. The product is working. Ros reports small things warmly, mentions the clinic's new tech, digresses about a difficult client with a cat named Governor. Priya is responsive but noticeably less so than during the crisis. One of the small things Ros mentions here is the same day-sheet printing bug, which she is now mentioning for the third time without framing it as a complaint.
constraints: the day sheet comes up a third time, in passing, unresolved
Priya's replies are warm but 40-70 words

threads.subject: Puyallup practice asked me about you
threads.beats: Late June. Rosalind unprompted offers to talk to other clinics, because a practice in Puyallup asked her what she uses. This is the payoff of the near-quit arc and should feel earned rather than sweet. She is matter-of-fact about it. Priya's reply is the most genuinely happy thing she writes in the corpus.
constraints: Rosalind does not make a big deal of it
Bramble is not mentioned, the warmth is elsewhere

threads.subject: Two people who failed at this
threads.beats: Marguerite delivers the two failure-story introductions she promised on Apr 6. Priya replies fast, 40 minutes, because this is an easy email. Reinforces that her latency with Marguerite is a function of the question and not the person.

threads.subject: Thicket monthly, May
threads.beats: The monthly update Priya promised. Long, good on product, quiet on customers, which is exactly the thing Marguerite calls out on Jun 8 in the metrics thread. Written at 12:40am on the last day of the month. Marguerite acknowledges briefly.
constraints: Priya's update is 300-400 words and mentions no revenue
sent after midnight on the last possible day

threads.subject: found this
threads.beats: A tiny warm thread with no ask in it. Wendy sends an old photo of the two of them at their grandfather's house. Priya replies within twenty minutes, which is the fastest she ever answers her sister, because there is nothing being asked of her. This thread is the control condition for the entire Wendy finding and it matters enormously: it proves the four-day gaps are not about Wendy.
constraints: no questions are asked by anyone
